role.altitude: The safety technician keeps designing drills, judging credentials and findings, educating and enforcing on site; digging up old drill reports, chasing certificates, copying findings from inspection reports and drafting materials from scratch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking extracted findings against the source report
role.ambitious_version: A technician who knows every open finding and expiring licence on any day and spends the time on site.

tasks.short: Review the emergency plan and last drill findings, design the drill scenario, schedule it, write the drill script and observer checklists, and brief observers to plan emergency response drills.

steps.what: Safety technician reviews the emergency plan, last drill findings and open actions
Safety technician plans the emergency response drill: scenario and objectives
Safety technician agrees the drill date with departments, the response team and building management
Safety technician checks the final drill invitation: date, building, what each group must do and the distribution list
Safety technician sends the checked drill invitation with its calendar slot to the building's distribution list
Safety technician writes the drill script and observer checklists
Safety technician briefs observers and the response team

tasks.design: Drill findings and their follow-up actions sit in the safety records app, so the technician sees the open points from earlier drills in one view instead of reading old reports. The drill invitation goes to fixed distribution lists per building with a calendar slot. Scripts and observer checklists start from earlier drills of the same type. Designing the scenario and briefing stay with the technician.

approvals.approved_version: The drill invitation with date, building, tasks per group and calendar slot exactly as checked by the technician in s3b, sent once to that building's distribution list; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Drill findings sat in old reports and spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Safety records apps with action tracking and drill templates.
tasks.still_hard: Departments that cannot spare time for a drill.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a scenario that tests the real weak point.
tasks.altitude: Less looking back and typing; design stays.

reach.learn: Whether open drill findings get closed.

evidence.claim: Employers keep a written risk inventory with an action plan.
Records apps with notifications replace action plans kept in spreadsheets.

assumptions: Boundary: planning drills; directing rescue operations (task 11100) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: drill findings and actions recorded in the safety records app after each drill.

Designing, briefing, checking and sending the invitation keep their full time. s3 keeps 75 because agreeing the date stays; fixed lists remove collecting addresses. s4 keeps 75 because the technician still writes the script for this scenario; earlier drills give the layout and standard roles.
research_questions: Are drill findings closed before the next drill?

incremental.description: Safety technician keeps distribution lists and drill templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few earlier drills of the same type are on record, so s4 keeps 90 and s1 keeps 80 (10.0); high: records and earlier drills as designed (17.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect certificates and licences, check validity and required types, examine credentials, licenses or permits for authenticity and scope, decide on non-compliance, and record outcomes and expiry follow-up.

steps.what: Contractor uploads certificates and licences to the contractor portal
Safety technician collects credentials, licences and permits from contractors and departments
Safety technician checks validity dates and required credential types per job
Safety technician examines credentials, licenses and permits for authenticity and scope to ensure compliance with licensing requirements
Safety technician decides on non-compliance: refuse access or escalate
Safety technician records the outcome and the access decision in the credential register
Safety technician checks the week's expiry reminder list: contractor, credential, expiry date and the reminder text
Safety technician sends the checked reminders from the register to the contractors
Safety technician follows up expiring credentials with contractors who do not renew

tasks.design: Contractors upload certificates and licences with their type and expiry date to a contractor portal before they get site access, instead of mailing copies. Rules check that each job has the required credential types and that none has expired. The technician examines the documents themselves for authenticity and scope and decides on non-compliance. The register lists credentials that expire soon; the technician checks the list and sends the reminders from it, and chases only those who do not renew. The outcome of each check stays a record the technician writes. Only the credential data needed for access are kept.

approvals.approved_version: The week's reminders with contractor, credential and expiry date exactly as checked by the technician in s6b, sent once from the register to those contractors; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Copies came by mail and expiry dates were tracked in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Contractor portals with credential registers and expiry reminders.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a certificate that has been altered.

ambition.what: Check credentials at every site entry instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: Less chasing and date checking; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether access is granted faster when credentials are current.

evidence.claim: Records apps with notifications replace credential lists in spreadsheets.
Systems that can monitor workers' behaviour or performance need works council consent; a credential register used only for access does not rate staff.

assumptions: Boundary: checking credentials for compliance; training workers (task 19818) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: contractors upload credentials in the portal, about 80% of them; the rest still mail copies; s2 is priced at that share.
Contractors' upload time is shown in s1 and is about what mailing copies took.
Examining, deciding, recording the outcome and checking reminders keep their full time. s6d keeps 30 for chasing contractors who do not renew; tracking dates in a spreadsheet goes.
research_questions: Do expired credentials on site fall?

incremental.description: Safety technician keeps the required credential types per job current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of contractors upload in the portal, so s2 keeps 69 and s3 keeps 60 (21.9); high: 80% upload as assumed (32.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect records and reports, extract findings and deadlines, review records or reports concerning laboratory results, staffing, floor plans, fire inspections or sanitation to judge needed safety activities, and update the risk action plan.

steps.what: Safety technician collects records and reports from departments and inspectors
Safety technician reads the reports and lists findings and deadlines

loop.input: Inspection reports, laboratory reports and sanitation reports as files.
loop.output: A list of findings with location, deadline and page reference.
loop.check: Each finding must quote its page; the technician reads the findings section of every report and checks that each listed finding and deadline says what the report says. Findings that do not match or are unclear are written by hand.
loop.stop: Reports that cannot be read are listed by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each inspector and laboratory uses its own report layout.

steps.what: Safety technician reviews the findings to judge which safety activities to develop or enforce and their priority
Safety technician writes the decided actions in the risk inventory action plan register with owners and due dates
Safety technician checks the final actions: what must be done, the owner, the due date and the finding each answers
Safety technician assigns the checked actions to their owners in the register

tasks.design: Departments and inspectors put their reports in a shared library by type and site, instead of the technician requesting them by mail. An extraction step lists findings with location, deadline and page reference, and the technician reads the findings section of every report. Judging what to act on stays with the technician. Decided actions go into the action plan register with owners, due dates and reminders. Medical details from laboratory reports about individual workers stay with the company doctor and are not copied into the plan.

approvals.approved_version: The actions with task, owner, due date and source finding exactly as checked by the technician in s4b, assigned once to those owners in the action plan register; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Reports arrived by mail in many layouts and findings were copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared report libraries, extraction with page references and action registers.
tasks.still_hard: Findings that point to a deeper problem across reports.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting a staffing gap to a sanitation finding.

ambition.what: Update the action plan after every report instead of once a quarter.

tasks.altitude: Less collecting and copying; judgement stays.

reach.learn: Whether actions are closed before their deadline.

evidence.claim: A maintenance firm was fined for recording the cause of employees' sickness, which belongs with the company doctor.
Employers keep a written risk inventory with an action plan.

assumptions: Boundary: reviewing reports for safety action; recommending corrective measures on contaminant analyses (task 20250) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: departments and the fire service's inspection reports placed in the shared library, about 70% of reports; s1 is priced at that share.

Judging, checking and assigning actions keep their full time. s4 keeps 80 because the register takes the finding, location and deadline from the findings list; the technician still writes each action and picks the owner.
research_questions: Are findings acted on before their deadlines?

already_counted.description: Safety technician corrects extracted findings that do not match the report.

incremental.description: Safety technician keeps report types and sites in the library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only 40% of reports reach the library and extraction fails on many layouts, so s1 keeps 72 and s2 keeps 80 (14.7); high: 70% in the library as assumed (25.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare information materials, check them, educate the public about health issues in talks, and enforce health legislation on site visits.

steps.what: Safety technician prepares information materials and presentations on health issues

loop.input: The relevant rules, the risk inventory and the technician's outline.
loop.output: Draft slides and a handout in plain language.
loop.check: Every rule or figure must cite its source paragraph; the technician checks each safety statement against the source.
loop.stop: The technician approves the material, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each audience needs a different level and focus.

steps.what: Safety technician checks and approves the final materials
Safety technician educates the public about health issues in talks and answers questions
Safety technician enforces health legislation on site visits

tasks.design: A drafting step writes slides and a plain-language handout from the relevant rules and the risk inventory, with each rule cited, and the technician checks every safety statement against its source before using it. Talks, answering questions and enforcing on site stay fully with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials were written from scratch for each audience.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from cited sources with expert review.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a business owner to fix a hazard.
tasks.altitude: Less writing; talking and enforcing stay.

evidence.claim: In a lab safety benchmark no model passed 70% accuracy at hazard identification, so model-written safety material needs expert review.
A safety product converts documents into inspection templates and translates training courses.

assumptions: Boundary: public health education and enforcement visits; conferring with schools and authorities on standards (task 11101) is a sibling task.
Talks, enforcement and the final check keep their full time. s1 keeps 75 because the technician still writes for the audience; the draft gives cited rules and layout.
research_questions: Do audiences remember the key rules better?

already_counted.description: Safety technician corrects drafted safety statements.

incremental.description: Safety technician keeps the source list for drafting current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: each audience needs its own material, so drafts are mostly rewritten and s1 keeps 90 (2.2); high: drafts as designed (5.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
